findings.reason: splitting the crew merge release into its own section gives each repair a done-when and a control of its own, and lets the already-built half land without waiting on the new path.
findings.text: §6 now carries two independent repairs: the post-merge receipt on `crew complete --land` (promotion_release.py, crew_run_commands.py) and a release path added to `crew merge` (merge.py), which is a different command, a different caller and a different defect (power-convertor-1f's run stayed a worktree-held obligation after the merge had pushed) — so one verdict cannot close the pair and the gate proves neither

findings.reason: removing the merge-side release would leave the fourth case red but no control asserts that, and the rubric's rule is that a node with no negative control cannot show its guard fires.
findings.text: §6's fourth case ("a run promoted by `crew complete` and landed by a separate `crew merge --head` has its worktree released by the merge") is the only evidence for the newly added merge release path and has no negative control: the two stated controls cover the first two cases only, so nothing shows the new guard fires

findings.reason: the site needs a predicate the plan does not name (an any-match over both directions, or `covered != set(after_ids)`), so as written the shared rule gives the wrong verdict at that site.
findings.text: §5's done-when states one assertion for all six sites ("a bare base name covering a qualified head id is not counted as added"), but the fifth-listed site, the retry-overlap test in reports.py near line 2653, is a symmetric intersection (`overlap = set(retry_failures) & after_ids`) and has no "added" figure to count; `failure_ids_covered(base, head)` returns the head ids the base does not cover, so with retry `{test_x}` and after `{tests/a.py::test_x, tests/b.py::test_y}` it returns a non-empty set while the ids do overlap, and a worker reading the deliverable literally would report no contradiction

findings.reason: review.py carries the shared predicate and the review-record writer, and a break there would pass this gate while breaking every downstream consumer.
findings.text: §5 changes `reckon/crew/review.py` (`added_failures_from_gate_logs`, `_retires_id`) and `reckon/crew/reports.py` (the retry-overlap test) but its regression clause requires "no failure against the base revision" only for "the test files importing `reckon.crew.promotion_checks`, `reckon.ledger` and `reckon.crew.landing_measure`", so a regression in the two largest files the section rewrites is outside its own measure

findings.reason: the deliverable is additive on the same function and no mechanism depends on the undercount, though the sentence should be corrected when §7 is next edited.
findings.text: §7's premise says `_require_gate_log_agrees` "refuses only an exit-status contradiction", but the function it cites (promotion_evidence.py:1062) refuses four shapes — an empty log, an exit-status contradiction, a command-not-found line with no positive record, and one more — as its own docstring and body show at lines 1093–1135

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — _require_gate_log_agrees (promotion_evidence.py:1062, exact), _recorded_exit_status (:1044, exact), _zero_added_against_a_red_base (:1174, exact), the promotion.py:573 lambda and _require_independently (promotion_checks.py:1355), gate_log_failure_ids (review.py:2106), _retires_id (review.py:2304), added_failures_from_gate_logs (review.py:2663), the ledgers and landing-measure sites, _record_release_on_ledger (:633), _release_after_promotion (:476), _release_run_workspace (:337), reports._terminal_exit_status (reports.py:1293) with its negative-control use at reports.py:2098.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §6's fourth case, the new crew merge release path, carries no negative control; and §5's done-when states one assertion shape ("not counted as added") for six sites, one of which is a symmetric overlap test that shape does not describe.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §6 places every log under the run directory, §7 records its census under the run directory, and §5's test artifacts are repository paths; none names a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers reach the symbols the three units add; the run ids and §-references are evidence, not code names.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §7's premise "refuses only an exit-status contradiction" does not match the function it cites.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §6 now carries two repairs, the post-merge release receipt on crew complete --land and a release added to crew merge, with separate code paths and no shared verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s5 depends-on s2, s7 depends-on s4 and s5, s8 depends-on s7, all declared in plan-section-depends-on; the write-path collisions land in dependency order (s5 and s7 both write review.py, s7 waits on s5; s5 changes reports.py and s8, which also writes reports.py, waits on s7 transitively).
